QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_64

answer.text: Putting investor interest first, providing complete information, and avoiding conflicts
Never saying anything negative about any AIF
Recommending to every person they meet

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM XIX-A (pp. 274, 276, 278), distributors must keep investor interest paramount, disclose full, latest and material information, avoid and disclose conflicts of interest, and maintain high standards of ethics, integrity and due diligence in their conduct. The Trap: Personal income, blanket positivity about every AIF, or indiscriminate recommendation all undermine the suitability and investor-first principles the workbook insists on. Note: Ethics is not about omitting negatives — it is about giving the investor the full picture, including risks, so they can make an informed decision.
